newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end flat despite interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end flat despite interest rate cut.

text.p: Australian shares closed barely changed on Wednesday after a widely-expected cut in Australian official interest rates failed to excite investors.
The maintenance of the political status quo in the United States after national elections also failed to stir interest and the All Ordinaries index closed a point lower at 2,360.6.

Some thought the Reserve Bank may have made a larger rate cut than that seen, but others suggested the 0.5 percentage point cut to 6.5 percent was appropriate and left the RBA with scope to cut again.
"I thought 0.5 was pretty well on the button and may leave the way open for another one not that far down the track," said head of equities at brokerage Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely.
Sekely noted that investors seemed comfortable with President Bill Clinton's re-election, given that the Republicans looked set to retain control of the Senate.
"He romped home and the Republicans won the Senate and that is about the ideal result," Sekely said.
General activity was unexciting in line with the moderate turnover levels.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 16 to 15, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
